record.paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
record.context_brief: continuous harmonic maps from B^3 to S^2
record.original_question: Let Omega be the unit ball B^3 in R^3. Given a smooth boundary map g: boundary Omega, identified with S^2, to S^2 with degree zero, consider weak harmonic maps u in H^1(Omega; R^3) satisfying Delta u_i = u_i |grad u|^2, |u|=1 in Omega, and u=g on the boundary. Does there always exist a continuous harmonic map satisfying this boundary value problem?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4.1 ([40, 41], [15, Open Problem 3]). Assume that deg g = 0. Does there exist a continuous harmonic map satisfying (4.1)-(4.3)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega = B^3 \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be the open unit ball, and identify its boundary $\partial\Omega$ with the unit sphere $S^2 \subset \mathbb{R}^3$. Let $g\colon S^2 \to S^2$ be a smooth map of topological degree $\deg g = 0$. Consider weak harmonic maps $u \in H^1(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^3)$ from $\Omega$ to $S^2$, that is, maps satisfying
\[ \Delta u_i = u_i\,|\nabla u|^2 \quad \text{in } \Omega \quad (i=1,2,3), \qquad |u(x)| = 1 \text{ for a.e. } x \in \Omega, \]
with the Dirichlet boundary condition $u = g$ on $\partial\Omega$ in the trace sense.

Question: Does there always exist a continuous map $u \in C^0(\overline{\Omega};S^2)$ that is a weak harmonic map and satisfies the boundary condition $u|_{\partial\Omega} = g$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether every smooth degree-zero boundary map $g\colon S^2\to S^2$ admits a continuous harmonic extension $u\colon \overline{B^3}\to S^2$ is a longstanding open problem in the theory of harmonic maps, going back to work of Hardt–Lin and others. Energy-minimizing extensions can have singularities even when $\deg g=0$, and various partial constructions exist, but no general existence theorem for continuous harmonic extensions in the degree-zero case is known. Web searches did not reveal a resolution.

status_evidence.title: Some new harmonic maps from B^3 to S^2
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions of harmonic maps B^3 -> S^2 with cylindrically symmetric boundary data of degree 0.
status_evidence.claim: Constructions of explicit harmonic maps with degree-zero boundary data exist, but a general continuous-existence theorem is not established.

status_evidence.title: Boundary regularity and the Dirichlet problem for harmonic maps (Hardt–Lin)
status_evidence.snippet: Boundary regularity results for harmonic maps and the Dirichlet problem.
status_evidence.claim: The Dirichlet problem for harmonic maps into S^2 has been studied but the degree-zero continuous existence question remains a recognized open problem.
